How we sell, in the open

Three rules, applied to every listing on this page — including the ones that make our job harder.

01

Priced from evidence

Every price starts from comparable sales within 500 metres, adjusted in writing. If we can't show the working, we don't print the number.

02

Flaws disclosed, in the listing

The worst thing about each home is on its card, in italics, before you visit. If we learn something new, the card changes the same day.

03

No auction theatre

Private treaty only. Written offers, a stated deadline, and the vendor's answer within one business day. No games, no phantom bidders.

Sold prices are the final contract prices — not the guides, not the hopes.

Book a viewing

Weekend inspections run 10:00–14:00; weekday viewings are evenings, 17:00–18:30. Pick a home, a day and a time — you'll get a booking code on the spot.

What happens next

  1. Your booking code appears here immediately — keep it for the door.
  2. We confirm by text within one business hour, from a number you can reply to.
  3. Running late or changed your mind? Change or cancel below — no phone call, no guilt trip.

Viewings run 30 minutes. The agent will point out the flaw from the listing first, then let you look around in peace.

Fair questions

Why publish the flaws? Doesn't that hurt the sale?

Buyers find the flaws anyway — at the building inspection, after they've paid for it. Publishing them early means the people who view a home already accept its worst feature, which is why our listings sell with fewer collapsed contracts.

Are the prices negotiable?

Every price is set from comparable sales and the working is available on request. Offers below the listed price are put to the vendor in writing, like any other — but the listed price is an honest one, not an opening bid.

Why no auctions?

Auctions reward theatre and punish preparation. We sell by private treaty: written offers, a stated deadline, and an answer within one business day. Calmer for buyers, and vendors get considered offers instead of adrenaline.

Can I view a home on a weekday?

Yes — weekday viewings run in the evening, 17:00–18:30, so you don't have to spend annual leave to stand in a kitchen. Weekend inspections run 10:00–14:00. Pick either in the booking form above.
